feed.title: Combined summary - Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?

entry.title: Combined summary - Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
entry.summary: Over the past two years, significant progress has been made in the management and development of the Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIP) repository. The BIP Editors processed 596 pull requests, merging 382 of these, and facilitated the publication of 42 new BIPs. Efforts included updating procedural documents, cleaning up abandoned submissions, refining continuous integration scripts, and implementing a new BIP Process. These actions contributed to a discernible increase in community engagement and submission activity within the repository. Despite these advancements, the workload distribution among editors revealed that a small core group was responsible for the majority of the contributions, with periods where only one editor managed most day-to-day responsibilities. This underscored the necessity for a sufficiently staffed editorial team. There is broad consensus that maintaining a smaller, highly active group—ideally three editors who are committed to regular participation—strikes an effective balance. Such a structure ensures sustainability and responsiveness without diluting accountability or engagement. Interest from new contributors has been welcomed, with prospective editors invited to share their qualifications to facilitate authorization. The primary qualifications for BIP Editors include experience with Bitcoin projects or protocol design, strong command of English, and an inclination toward meticulous, detail-oriented work. The role typically demands a commitment of at least 5 to 10 hours per week, encompassing routine tasks such as monitoring open pull requests, encouraging timely reviews and updates, and merging completed work. For modifications to existing BIPs, editors rely on input from original authors, while for new proposals, thorough technical assessment and constructive feedback are essential. The editorial process remains largely accessible; community members are encouraged to review and comment on open pull requests ([see current open PRs](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Apr+-label%3A%22Metadata+Update%22+-label%3ATypo-to-be-collected+-label%3ACI)). Active, meaningful participation in reviewing and providing feedback not only supports the repository’s ongoing maintenance but also positions contributors for consideration as future editors. Recent discussions highlight the challenge of keeping pace with the volume of incoming submissions, especially during periods when editors are unavailable due to personal commitments. Two possible pathways were identified: expanding the number of active editors or lowering review standards to focus mainly on format rather than substantive content. The preferred approach is to maintain high standards by ensuring the editorial team consists of three regularly contributing members. Flexibility in commitment is acknowledged, allowing volunteers to serve fixed terms of 12 to 24 months if desired. In conclusion, sustaining a vibrant, well-managed BIP process depends on active participation from both editors and community reviewers. Ongoing recruitment and clear guidelines for involvement aim to ensure the continued growth and integrity of the Bitcoin protocol’s improvement process.
